# First public release

Common Measure rules on which content an AI agent may take in, records where
each piece came from and what it cost, and measures whether it helped. This
is the first release anyone can download and run without an account. The
source is available under the Functional Source License, FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0,
which converts to Apache-2.0 two years after each release; the protocol
contracts and evidence format specifications under `docs/contracts/` are
CC-BY-4.0, so anyone may implement the formats regardless of the code
licence.

## What the release holds

- `commonmeasure-linux-x64`, `commonmeasure-linux-arm64`,
  `commonmeasure-darwin-arm64`, `commonmeasure-darwin-x64` and
  `commonmeasure-win-x64.exe`: one prebuilt `commonmeasure` binary per
  supported platform, named as the plugin's launcher names them.
- `commonmeasure-plugin-0.3.0.tar.gz`: the Claude Code plugin as its own
  marketplace, bundling all five binaries.
- `install.sh`: the installer.
- `SHA256SUMS`: the SHA-256 of every other asset.

## Installing

The installer needs `curl` and `sha256sum` or `shasum`, and no account:

```sh
curl -fsSL -o install.sh https://github.com/commonmeasure/commonmeasure/releases/download/v0.3.0/install.sh
sh install.sh --tag v0.3.0
```

It downloads this platform's binary with the checksum list, verifies the
checksum before the binary is placed in `~/.local/bin`, and checks that the
installed binary reports this version. `--plugin DIR` also unpacks the
plugin archive into `DIR` and prints the two commands that install it into
Claude Code. Verify any other download with
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` from the directory the files are
in.

To register the installed binary with a host directly:

```sh
commonmeasure install claude
```

To install the plugin from this repository as a Claude Code marketplace,
with the binary already installed:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add commonmeasure/commonmeasure
claude plugin install commonmeasure@commonmeasure
```

## What it does once installed

Every crossing, the moment content from outside enters the agent's working
context, is recorded on the operator's own machine: observed after the fact
for the host's own fetch and search tools, or mediated through the
product's `context_fetch` and `context_search` tools, where deterministic
policy can refuse it first. `commonmeasure session` prints what the current
session retrieved and grounded on; `commonmeasure serve` starts the console
on loopback. Nothing leaves the machine unless the operator configures a
receiver and clears an engagement for reporting.

## Verified on this release

The installer and the plugin archive are exercised on Linux in a container
with no toolchain and no credential, and the macOS Apple Silicon binary is
built and run on the same kind of machine. The Linux arm64, macOS Intel
and Windows binaries are built and checksummed by the same run; the
installer has not been run on Windows.

## Known limitations

The committed demonstration runs under `demo/output` were recorded on a
developer machine and carry that machine's file paths. They are
hash-sealed as recorded and will be regenerated in a later release.
